observed_facts.statement: The archived run log contains 42504 DEBUG lines and 6 INFO lines (7573160 bytes total), predominantly Hikari connection-adder diagnostics. No WARN or ERROR record was found.

The pinned code uses Ktor CIO and performs synchronous JDBC operations on Dispatchers.IO through Hikari. Database setup requests WAL, synchronous=NORMAL and busy_timeout=5000 via connectionInitSql; source does not explicitly override Hikari pool size.
Post-stop quick_check returnedok and post count increased. Container remained running and reported no OOM kill. These checks do not identify why one request timed out.

The saved log contains no SQLITE_BUSY/database-is-locked line, timeout exception, OOM message, GC-pause record or Hikari starvation warning. There is no request-level record linking the single client timeout to an endpoint, query, pool wait or JVM event.

inferences.confidence: consistent with observations, causal attribution not established
inferences.statement: Near-full CPU usage and observed pool waiting provide plausible queueing context for a rare long request. The substantialDEBUG logging may add work, but the saved evidence does not prove that pool waiting, logging, SQLite locking, JIT/GC, scheduling or any specific component caused this single timeout.
